summary: Clock-drift-induced 429s during multi-AZ burst in eu-west-1
description: Issue summary: BrightWrite reported repeated 429 throttling errors during a scheduled background prefetch job that runs across multiple AZs. Impact: customer observed degraded throughput for realtime chat requests and failed bulk embedding prefetch jobs for ~15 minutes. Environment: Dedicated tenant on eu-west-1, using a mix of short-lived upload workers and streaming chat clients. Steps to reproduce: 1) Start staggered prefetch workers across three AZs (A/B/C) with overlapping burst windows. 2) Rotate ephemeral keys every 30s for the upload fleet. 3) Trigger a short realtime chat session concurrently. Observed behavior: Tenants received 429s that appeared to exhaust the tenant token bucket faster than expected; 429s correlated with the burst but occurred even when aggregate token counts should have allowed the requests. Expected behavior: Token buckets should be refilled consistently across AZs, preventing premature 429s during short, multi-AZ bursts. Logs and traces: - Edge gateway logs show refill timestamps with up to 1.5s skew between AZs. - Rate limiter metrics show near-simultaneous debit events from different gateways within the same logical refill window. - No application-level spike in legitimate token usage beyond what the customer reported.
comments: 2026-03-10T09:04Z - Asha Patel (Support): Initial report received from BrightWrite: multiple 429s starting ~09:00 UTC, lasting ~15m. Attached sample request IDs and client IPs.
2026-03-10T09:30Z - Samir Gupta (SRE): Scoped to api-gateway/rate-limiter. Noting refill timestamp differences across AZs; opened INT-1442 to run clock check across edge fleet.
2026-03-10T10:02Z - BrightWrite (Customer): Confirmed they perform a coordinated prefetch job and key rotation. Provided timing window and worker counts.

2026-03-11T01:18Z - Samir Gupta (SRE): Deployed temporary mitigation: force-coordinated-token-window (feature flag) in eu-west-1 to align refill acceptance for tenant buckets; results showing reduction in 429s for subsequent test bursts.
2026-03-12T12:40Z - Diego Morales (Platform Engineer): Proposed permanent fix in rate-limiter to use monotonic time and tolerate 2s of cross-node drift. Created PR and scheduled canary rollout.

investigation_notes: Hypothesis 1: Clock skew across edge gateway instances caused refill window misalignment, resulting in overlapping debit windows and double-counting of available tokens.
Hypothesis 2: Ephemeral key rotation created short-lived parallel sessions that coincided with the skewed refill times, increasing perceived concurrency.

Evidence: NTP/chrony metrics show a group of gateways in eu-west-1 drifting by up to 1.4s after a vendor maintenance window. Trace correlation IDs show identical tenant bucket IDs being debited by two gateways within 500ms to 1.2s of each other.
Repro steps executed in sandbox: Simulated 3-AZ burst with controlled 1.2s clock offsets; observed 429 spike matching customer report.
Temporary mitigation validated: enabling force-coordinated-token-window reduced 429 rate in controlled test by ~92% for same load profile.

Next actions: schedule fleet-wide chrony restart, roll the monotonic-clock rate-limiter patch through canary, update runbook to check clock health after maintenance windows, and add observability alert for >250ms median clock skew across gateways.
Related internal ticket: INT-1442 (edge clock health sweep) for postmortem and runbook changes.
resolution: Mitigation: rolled a temporary feature-flag 'force-coordinated-token-window' in eu-west-1 and asked customer to avoid key rotations during scheduled bursts. Root cause: NTP drift on a subset of edge gateways after maintenance caused refill-window misalignment; this exposed a timing sensitivity in the token-bucket implementation. Permanent fix: rate-limiter change to use monotonic clocks and tolerate small cross-node drift was merged and is in canary rollout as of 2026-03-12. Follow-ups: fleet chrony restart, new alerting for clock skew, update runbook, and a postmortem to be published after canary completes. Customer-facing note: customer was given rollback/migration guidance and a recommended backoff pattern (exponential with jitter) until the permanent fix is in prod.
